question.worked_solution:
If we attempt to evaluate the limit, we get an indeterminate form:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to -1}\frac{{t}^{2}-8t-9}{{t}^{2}-5t-6} & =\frac{(-1)^{2}-8(-1)-9}{(-1)^{2}-5(-1)-6}=\frac{0}{0}\end{aligned}
$$

So, to find the limit, we have to factor the numerator and the denominator. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{t}^{2}-8t-9}{{t}^{2}-5t-6} & =\frac{(t+1)(t-9)}{(t+1)(t-6)} \\  & =\frac{t-9}{t-6}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{t\to -1}\frac{{t}^{2}-8t-9}{{t}^{2}-5t-6} & ={lim}_{t\to -1}\frac{t-9}{t-6} \\  & =\frac{-1-9}{-1-6} \\  & =\frac{(-10)}{(-7)} \\  & =\frac{10}{7}.\end{aligned}
$$
